notes.title: App sandbox
notes.text: An app can’t harm your site. Every app runs in a sandbox and reads only the site data it asks for. Open an app and look under Permissions to see where it runs and how much access it has.
A site’s own CSS that uses the theme’s color, shape and elevation variables must switch to the new variable names, which start with --mo-
Apps can add their own widgets to the start screen

notes.title: Start screen widgets
notes.text: Your start screen shows what matters to you. Widgets sit in a grid: Continue, Unfinished, Blog rhythm and Site status. Tap Edit dashboard to add, remove and reorder them.

notes.title: Editions
notes.text: Each update is easy to recognize. It comes with a photo and the name of the place it’s named after, like Passo Giau. You’ll find them on the start screen and on the Morpheme page.
The sort and filters you last chose when you pick pages or items start fresh once
The downloaded consent log is now named consents-<date>.csv
New versions of your pages are now at /new/, and old links keep working
A tag’s page on your blog is now at /blog/tags/<tag>/, and links to the old address keep working
The text toolbar and the menu over selected text have the same heading and text buttons

notes.title: Color names
notes.text: Colors use Material 3’s own names. Open Colors and save to switch your old ones over; they keep working until you do. New are Surface dim, Surface bright, Scrim and Shadow.
Versions 0.2 to 0.13 now have release notes and a photo on the Morpheme page
Only one Redirects app and one Links app can be on at a time, and a second one asks first

notes.title: Page settings
notes.text: A page’s basics sit in one place. Open a page and tap Page settings to set its title, status and template, and pick the template on cards.
A site can post each new Morpheme release on its blog by itself
Your site updates to this version with the Update button, with no extra npm command

notes.title: Settings cog
notes.text: The menu stays short. Tap the cog at the bottom of the menu to open Settings, with Appearance, Developer, Licenses, Morpheme and Privacy.
The buttons under Notifications are now Clear and Settings
Appstore has 13 categories to filter by
Each version on the Morpheme page shows its date and photo
